rule_needed: Subtract preferred at its liquidation value (not par) plus all cumulative dividends in arrears, including the current year, from total equity; divide the rest by common shares outstanding.

Remeasure the asset to fair value at the declaration date and book the gain or loss in income; the dividend is recorded at that fair value, so the net hit to retained earnings equals the asset's carrying value.
Stock splits and stock dividends are applied retroactively to all shares outstanding before them, as if they happened at the start of the year; they are not time-weighted from the split date.
Days sales in A/R = ending net A/R ÷ (net sales ÷ 365); average A/R is used for A/R turnover, not for this ratio.

Sales are net of discounts and never include gains; a gain on sale of equipment goes under other revenues and gains, and depreciation is an operating expense. Tax expense on the face is the rate times pretax income from continuing operations, and discontinued operations are shown net of their own tax.

A change from LIFO is applied retrospectively: beginning retained earnings is adjusted by the inventory difference at the beginning of the period, net of tax; the year-end difference doesn't set the cumulative effect.
